annotations.title: Index Fund Flows and Rebalance Trades

description: Get the money flowing into or out of the fund that tracks an index, and what that fund bought and sold for the index at its last rebalance. Covers the indexes whose tracking fund publishes a daily holdings file, such as the S&P 500 (IVV), S&P MidCap 400 (IJH), S&P SmallCap 600 (IJR), Russell 1000 (IWB) and Russell 2000 (IWM). A flow is an estimate: creating or redeeming units scales every holding alike, so the median change in the fund's share counts between two daily files is its flow, applied to the fund's value. It is that one fund's money, not demand for the index. A rebalance is the newest session where at least one holding in ten moved more than 2% apart from the fund's flow; those holdings were traded for the index itself. The trade lists rank every holding more than 0.1% apart from the flow by dollar value, so a small adjustment to a large company can lead them. Use GetIndexChanges for the companies that joined or left.

index.description: Index name or slug, for example "S&P 500", "sp-500", "S&P MidCap 400" or "Russell 2000".
